diagnosis_explanation:
Your lungs got irritated and infected. This happened because food or liquid went into your lungs by mistake. We call this aspiration pneumonia.

You also have a lung condition called COPD. This makes breathing harder. Sometimes COPD can get worse. This can make breathing very difficult.

Your breathing was not good enough for your body. This was because of your COPD getting worse. Your body also had trouble breathing out carbon dioxide.

Your heart had a fast or irregular beat. We were able to get it back to a normal rhythm.

You have high blood sugar. This is related to your diabetes. You need insulin for this.

You have high blood pressure. It is now controlled well.

You also have high cholesterol.

Your kidneys were not working well for a time. They are now working fine again.
medication_rationale:
Home oxygen:
This medicine gives you extra oxygen to breathe. It helps your body get the oxygen it needs. You may feel more comfortable breathing. This is a sign it is working well. There are no side effects to watch for.

Ativan:
This medicine helps you feel calm and relaxed. It can help with breathing problems. You may feel sleepy or a little dizzy. This is normal and should pass. Call your doctor if you feel too drowsy or confused.

Metformin:
This medicine helps control your blood sugar. It is for diabetes. You may have an upset stomach. This is common when you start. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or feel very weak.

Glucotrol:
This medicine helps lower your blood sugar. It is for diabetes. You may feel dizzy or shaky. This can happen if your blood sugar gets too low. Eat something if you feel this way. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Spiriva:
This medicine helps you breathe easier. It opens up your airways. You may notice your mouth feels dry. This is a common side effect. Call your doctor if you have trouble urinating or feel dizzy.

Lantus:
This medicine is a type of insulin. It helps control your blood sugar. It is for diabetes. You might have redness or swelling where you inject it. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if your blood sugar gets too low. Symptoms include shaking or sweating.

Cardizem CD:
This medicine helps your heart pump better. It also lowers blood pressure. You may feel tired or dizzy. This is common. Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy or your heart beats too slowly.

Advair:
This medicine helps open your airways. It makes it easier to breathe. You may get a headache or feel shaky. This is not usually serious. Rinse your mouth after using it. Call your doctor if your breathing gets worse.

Iron:
This medicine helps your body make more red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen. You may have constipation or an upset stomach. Drink plenty of water. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain.

Aspirin:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. It can also reduce pain and fever. You may have an upset stomach. Taking it with food can help. Call your doctor if you have black, tarry stools or severe stomach pain.

Lipitor:
This medicine helps lower your cholesterol. High cholesterol can harm your heart. You may have muscle aches. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you have severe muscle pain or weakness.

Digoxin:
This medicine helps your heart pump blood better. It can also help control your heart rhythm. You may feel dizzy or sick to your stomach. Call your doctor if you have vision changes or feel very weak.

Lisinopril:
This medicine helps relax your blood vessels. This lowers your blood pressure. You may develop a dry cough. This is a common side effect. Call your doctor if your face or lips swell.

DuoNeb:
This medicine helps you breathe easier. It relaxes the muscles around your airways. You may feel shaky or have a faster heart rate. This is common. Call your doctor if your breathing gets worse.

Prednisone:
This medicine reduces swelling in your body. It is for inflammation. You may feel more hungry or have trouble sleeping. You may also get a sore throat. Call your doctor if you have mood changes or severe stomach pain.

Clindamycin:
This medicine fights a bacterial infection. It is for pneumonia. You may have an upset stomach or diarrhea. Call your doctor if you have severe diarrhea or a rash.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel very tired and weak.
- You can walk from your bed to the bathroom.
- Use your home oxygen as directed, 1 to 2 liters.
- Eat soft foods and thick liquids. Thin liquids are okay.
- Call your doctor if you have severe shortness of breath.
- Your goal this week is to rest and heal.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy.
- Try to walk a little more each day inside your home.
- Continue to use your home oxygen at 1 to 2 liters.
- Stick to your Dysphagia 2 diet. Thin liquids are okay.
- Call your doctor if you have severe shortness of breath.
- Your goal this week is to walk to your mailbox.

**Week 3:**
- You might feel less pain and more comfortable.
- You can do light activities around the house.
- Keep using your oxygen at 1 to 2 liters.
- Continue your Dysphagia 2 diet. Thin liquids are okay.
- Call your doctor if you have severe shortness of breath.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel stronger and have more energy each day.
- You can increase your walking time slowly.
- Continue using your oxygen as prescribed, 1 to 2 liters.
- Eat your Dysphagia 2 diet. Thin liquids are okay.
- Call your doctor if you have severe shortness of breath.
- Your goal this week is to walk around your block once.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Recovery takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Continue to follow all diet and oxygen instructions.
- Keep up with your walking and activity as you feel able.
- Call your doctor if you have any concerns.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Severe shortness of breath: You may not be getting enough oxygen.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever above 101 degrees: You may have an infection.
- Confusion or disorientation, new and worsening: This needs quick checks.
- Fast heart rate that returns: Your heart rhythm may be unstable.
- Coughing up thick, discolored mucus: This could mean a bad infection.
- Chest pain or pressure that will not stop: Your lungs may be strained.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Trouble breathing that is slowly improving: You still need monitoring.
- Mild body aches: This can happen as you recover.
- Feeling tired and weak: Your body needs time to heal.
- Questions about your medicines: Your doctor can clarify doses.
